deep.reconstruction:
Context (cote 148, 1983; this is p.18 of Grothendieck's own numbering). The notes study groupoids of compact topological surfaces X with boundary, possibly orientation-reversing morphisms (the superscript ±). The surfaces carry a 'découpage', a family of cutting circles C_a, and structures R: subgroups or torsors of Z_a/r_aZ attached to the circles, encoding 'repères' (boundary rigidifications) up to r_a-fold ambiguity. Combinatorially, each object has a 'bipondéré' dual graph Γ (Gr.pond.typ): genus weights at vertices, weights r_a on the edges. The previous page lists seven elementary operations between such objects:
0° direct sum.
1° erasing repères.
2°/3° restriction or extension of the Z/r_a structure (change of level r'_a | r_a).
4° erasing cutting circles.
5° capping holes.
6° dilatations along C_a.
7° regluing two boundary circles with equal r via an element of R_a ∧ R_a'.

This page states a wished-for 'petit théorème de dévissage préliminaire'. Up to equivalence (unique up to unique isomorphism), the big groupoid S_A T D^±_typ is determined by local data. This includes its functors Γ to typical weighted graphs and X̄ to [±1] (orientation character), and the elementary operations 1°–5° and their simultaneous composites. A margin correction restricts this to 'except 4° and 5°'. The local data are, for each type (g,ν), the tower
S_1T^±_{g,ν} → T^±_{g,ν} → Ens(ν)×[±1].
Here T^±_{g,ν} is the (extended) Teichmüller groupoid of connected surfaces of genus g with ν boundary components. The second map records the permutation of boundary components and orientation behaviour. S_1T^±_{g,ν} is the subgroupoid of the structured objects (X,R) with R∩C_a = 1 for every boundary component, i.e. boundary fully rigidified ('poids 1'). Equivalently, the weighted graph is a single vertex of genus g with ν legs of weight 1.

In modern terms: the groupoid of decorated surfaces with a cut system is reconstructed as a kind of Grothendieck construction over the category of weighted dual graphs. The fibres are products over vertices of the vertex mapping-class groupoids with boundary framing. They are extended by the twist and level data on edges and by graph automorphisms. This is the groupoid form of the classical structure of a multicurve stabiliser in the (extended) mapping class group. The operations that change topology (4° erasing circles, 5° capping) cannot be read off from the vertex groupoids alone. The next page says 4° will follow from the explicit description of T^±_top(Γ), and 5° from 'standard elementary' special cases for small (g,ν). This is the 'Lego' / Teichmüller-tower philosophy later announced in the Esquisse d'un programme (1984).
errors: No mathematical error. The marginal restriction 'à l'exception de 4° et 5°' is necessary: gluing and capping operations involve genuinely new relations (the later 'Lego' relations in low (g,ν)) and are not determined by the vertex groupoids alone. Grothendieck evidently realised this while writing.
The theorem is only stated as a programme; no proof or precise statement of the equivalence (2-categorical data, compatibility of the [±1] characters on edges) is given.

ideas.what: Dévissage: the groupoid of decorated surfaces with a cut system and its elementary operations is reconstructed from the vertex Teichmüller groupoids T^±_{g,ν} with boundary rigidification S_1T^±_{g,ν}, over weighted dual graphs.
ideas.modern_name: Structure of stabilisers of multicurves in the mapping class group; modular operad / graph-indexed (Grothendieck-construction) description of Teichmüller groupoids
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birman–Lubotzky–McCarthy and Ivanov (multicurve stabilisers, 1980s); modular operads: Getzler–Kapranov (1998)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §§2–3 (Teichmüller tower, 'jeu de Lego'), in philosophical form without this formalism

ideas.what: Fibration tower S_1T_{g,ν} → T_{g,ν} → Ens(ν)×[±1]: boundary-framed groupoid over the full groupoid over boundary permutations and orientation character.
ideas.modern_name: Framed / pure / full extended mapping class groupoids and their exact sequences (boundary Dehn twists, permutation of punctures, orientation reversal)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Birman; capping and boundary exact sequences)

ideas.what: Weighted ('bipondéré') dual graphs with genus at vertices and level r_a on edges, with structures R_a ⊂ Z/r_a at cut circles changed by restriction or extension (operations 2°, 3°).
ideas.modern_name: Stable graphs with twisting / level data at nodes (cf. twisted stable curves with μ_r at nodes)

missed.claim: The combinatorial apparatus in the Teichmüller notes resembles the later theory of twisted stable curves, where nodes carry μ_r-stabilisers and 'balanced' gluing data. That apparatus is: cut circles carrying Z/r_a structures, level change r'_a | r_a, and gluing two circles with r_a = r_a' via an element of R_a ∧ R_a'. The resemblance is a plausible anticipation, not an established equivalence. The page shows the plan of making this graph-indexed and functorial in Γ.
missed.quote: avec les foncteurs Γ dans (Gr.pond. typ) et X̄ dans [±1] ... se reconstitue par la connaissance des groupoïdes et foncteurs suivants
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The analogy could inform a topological / groupoid model of the boundary strata of moduli of twisted (orbifold) curves. It could also help track the action of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group on towers with level structure.

missed.claim: A precise 'dévissage' theorem: the 2-groupoid of all typical decorated surfaces, with operations 1°–3°, 6°, 7°, is equivalent to a construction built from the vertex towers S_1T^±_{g,ν} → T^±_{g,ν} → Ens(ν)×[±1] over the category of weighted graphs. This includes orientation-reversing morphisms. The theorem was never written out. Later Lego results (Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Bakalov–Kirillov, Funar–Gelca) treat the orientation-preserving, level-free case.
missed.quote: Il faudrait expliciter un petit théorème de dévissage préliminaire
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: An extended (±) version with level structures at edges is not standard in the literature, as far as I know.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is mostly a programmatic plan in the spirit of the Esquisse's Teichmüller Lego. Two details are less standard: the inclusion of orientation-reversing morphisms and of Z/r level data on cut circles within a functorial graph-indexed framework. The underlying mathematics (multicurve stabilisers) is classical.
transcription_corrections: Page number at top is '18' (sequence 17, 18, 19), not '15'.
'Π_0 ∂X = ν' should be read as card Π_0(∂X) = ν (ν boundary components).
In the next-page transcription '$\mathcal{T}' should be S T (the S-decorated groupoid), not a dollar sign.

Left margin likely reads: 'pour un petit peu tout à fait, pour avoir toutes les opérations. Notamment les opérations (4°) (pour avoir l'intérieur des T) de restriction ; (5°) des T_{g,ν}'; reading uncertain.
'bilisses' near the graph drawing is uncertain; possibly 'libres' or 'bilatères'.
